$comment: Czech public holidays (státní a ostatní svátky). "date" is MM-DD, or "easter-2" / "easter+1" for Good Friday and Easter Monday (computed). "shops": closed by law for larger shops, "noon" = closed from midday, "open". Matches the culture guide (holidays.md).

source.title: Dates: Ministry of Foreign Affairs list of public holidays 2026 (Act 245/2000 Coll.; later amendments 279/2024 and 59/2026 add commemorative days only). Shops: Czech Trade Inspection Authority (ČOI) press release of 19 Dec 2025 on Act 223/2016 Coll.

holidays.cs: Den obnovy samostatného českého státu · Nový rok
holidays.about: The Czech Republic began on 1 January 1993, and it's New Year's Day.
The day of the pomlázka: boys go round with braided willow whips, and get painted eggs.
Labour Day, and the traditional day for lovers to kiss under a blossoming tree.
The end of the Second World War in Europe, 1945.

holidays.cs: Den slovanských věrozvěstů Cyrila a Metoděje
holidays.about: The two missionaries who brought Christianity and writing to the Slavs in 863.
The church reformer Jan Hus was burned at the stake on this day in 1415.
The feast of St Wenceslas (svatý Václav), patron saint of the Czech lands.
Czechoslovakia was founded on 28 October 1918: the main national day.

holidays.cs: Den boje za svobodu a demokracii
holidays.en: Struggle for Freedom and Democracy Day
holidays.about: The student protests of 1939 and the Velvet Revolution of 1989. People light candles on Národní třída.
The day of Czech Christmas: carp for dinner, and presents from Ježíšek in the evening.
Visiting family and friends, or a walk off the cukroví.

shopsNote: The ban covers shops with more than 200 m² of sales floor. Shops at train and bus stations and airports, pharmacies, petrol stations and shops in hospitals may stay open.
